House Price Prediction

I explored which property features could support a useful sale-price estimate, then connected a trained model to a six-input Streamlit form.

Pythonpandasscikit-learnXGBoostStreamlit
Explore the repository ↗
Problem

Why this project?

I wanted to see how a regression model trained on Ames Housing could be used through a short form. A small input set makes the app easy to try and makes the cost of leaving out other pricing factors visible.

Approach

From input to output.

I used a notebook to prepare features, explore Random Forest and XGBoost, and use cross-validation during model tuning. I saved the trained XGBoost model and connected it to a Streamlit form with the same six inputs.

Workflow illustration
01Property features
02Feature preparation
03Trained XGBoost model
04Price estimate

A simplified overview of the repository’s application flow.

Implementation
01

Training workspace

A dedicated notebook separates model development from the prediction interface.

02

Six input features

The application uses total square footage, lot area, year built, bedrooms above ground, total bathrooms, and garage capacity.

03

Interactive prediction

The Streamlit form passes the six property fields to the trained XGBoost model and displays an estimate. The repository includes instructions for running the app.

What I learned and what to keep in mind

The form made the connection between feature engineering and usability concrete. Each field needed to be understandable to a visitor and match what the model expected. The estimate reflects the Ames Housing training data and works as a demonstration of the model.
